cards.back: A limit describes the value f(x) approaches as x approaches a target.
steps: Check left-hand and right-hand behavior near that x-value.
If both sides approach the same value L, limit equals L.
If sides differ, the two-sided limit does not exist.
cards.tip: Tip: Limits ask about approach behavior, not necessarily the exact function value at the point.
hints: Look near the x-value from both left and right.
If left and right approach different values, stop: no two-sided limit.
If both sides agree, that common value is the limit even if f(a) is undefined.
cards.example: In traffic modeling, speed near a merge point can approach a value even if one sensor reading exactly at that point is missing.

cards.back: f is continuous at a if f(a) exists, lim x->a f(x) exists, and they are equal.
steps: Compute left and right limits at x = a to confirm limit exists.
Conclude continuity only if all three checks pass.
cards.tip: Tip: Continuity checklist is D-L-E: Defined, Limit exists, Equal values.
hints: Continuity is a three-check process, not one.
Check value at a and limit at a separately first.
Only call it continuous when defined, limit exists, and both match.
cards.example: A smooth production-rate graph is continuous when there are no sudden jumps between consecutive time measurements.

cards.back: If y = f(g(x)), then y' = f'(g(x))*g'(x).

cards.front: Derivative of e^x and ln x
cards.back: d/dx[e^x] = e^x and d/dx[ln x] = 1/x for x>0.
Use when x and y are mixed in one equation and y is not isolated.
Critical points occur where f'(x)=0 or f'(x) is undefined and x is in domain.
Sign change of f' from + to - indicates local max; - to + indicates local min.
f''>0 means concave up, f''<0 means concave down.
If f is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), some c has f'(c)=[f(b)-f(a)]/(b-a).
If F'(x)=f(x), then F is an antiderivative of f.
Integral accumulates net signed area between curve and x-axis.
If F(x)=integral from a to x of f(t)dt, then F'(x)=f(x).
Integral from a to b of f(x)dx = F(b)-F(a), where F' = f.
Use substitution when integrand includes a function and its derivative pattern.
